findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the raw `datetime` value of AuditLogEntry, so build_cursor raises TypeError on every non-empty page: the "optimized" path can never return a successful response and 500s for any admin who sets ?optimized_pagination=true

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — Comment claims "Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" but QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.") for any negative start/stop; the entire advanced-features branch is unreachable-as-success and a reliable crash vector (cursor=0:-1:0) for org owners/managers with has_global_access

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally (before checking the query flag); RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is None for non-member callers (API keys, org auth tokens, non-member superusers fail only if is_superuser is False) so the whole endpoint 500s with AttributeError for those principals even without ?optimized_pagination

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — start/end/statsPeriod params and the datetime__range filter were silently removed; the non-strict serializer ignores unknown keys, so existing clients requesting a date window now receive the full unfiltered audit history with a 200, a silent feature regression unrelated to the stated performance goal

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Documented `start`, `end`, `statsPeriod` query params were removed from AuditLogQueryParamSerializer and the date-range filter deleted on a published (EXPERIMENTAL) endpoint; existing callers sending these params now silently receive unfiltered results (no 400, no deprecation path).

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the `datetime` field value, which raises TypeError (verified: "must be real number, not datetime.datetime"), so any `optimized_pagination=true` request with results 500s while building Link-header cursors.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:842 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of decoding the ms-float that DateTimePaginator emits, so cursors are not interchangeable between the two modes of the same endpoint and a DateTimePaginator-issued cursor is compared against the datetime column as a bare number.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — New `optimized_pagination` query flag is read straight from request.GET, bypassing AuditLogQueryParamSerializer, and is undocumented; it silently changes pagination semantics based on caller privilege with no schema or docs update.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — Negative cursor offsets are now accepted as a public cursor input (`cursor=<v>:-N:0`) and passed to Django slicing, which raises AssertionError ("Negative indexing is not supported") and surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400 for malformed cursors.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator now clamps negative non-prev offsets to 0 for every cursor-paginated endpoint, silently returning page 0 where a malformed cursor previously errored; this is an unannounced cross-endpoint behavior change.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on a datetime (audit log key is "datetime"), raising TypeError in build_cursor for any non-empty page

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value which build_queryset injects into a raw SQL `datetime <= %s` comparison, producing a Postgres type error for any cursor with a value

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — Negative cursor.offset is passed directly to queryset[start:stop]; Django QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported"), so the "advanced" branch always 500s instead of paginating

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member is None for non-member users (e.g. superusers or org-scoped tokens), so `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError whenever request.user.is_superuser is False

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — start/end/statsPeriod query params and the datetime__range filter were removed, so date-filtered requests now silently return unfiltered results

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator still passes a negative offset to the slice when cursor.is_prev, so a crafted prev cursor with negative offset raises ValueError (500) while the same offset on a next cursor is silently clamped to 0

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:891 — Trailing-row trim uses `offset + limit + extra` while results were fetched from start_offset..start_offset+limit+extra; when offset is negative the condition can never match and the extra row is not dropped

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — Gating a "privileged" pagination mode on `has_global_access` (true for ordinary org owners/managers, not just superusers) and a user-supplied `optimized_pagination` flag is security theater: it neither restricts nor protects anything, while suggesting that negative offsets are a privileged capability; the feature flag should not be user-controlled and the branch should be removed.

There are no visible changes in this diff showing removal of `start`, `end`, or `statsPeriod` parameters, nor removal of a `datetime__range` filter. It does not show any changes to `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer`, documented `start/end/statsPeriod` params, or any removal of date-range filtering logic. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the `datetime` field value, which raises TypeError (verified: "must be real number, not datetime.datetime"), so any `optimized_pagination=true` request with results 500s while building Link-header cursors.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key`, it does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` to `value` and casts to `int`. In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the optimized path paginates audit log rows ordered by `-datetime` (and does not override the paginator key), so the key is plausibly the `datetime` field. Applying `math.floor/ceil` to a `datetime` object will raise a `TypeError`, causing 500s when building cursors/Link headers for `optimized_pagination=true` requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:842 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of decoding the ms-float that DateTimePaginator emits, so cursors are not interchangeable between the two modes of the same endpoint and a DateTimePaginator-issued cursor is compared against the datetime column as a bare number.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor simply returns cursor.value, but it does not show how DateTimePaginator encodes/decodes cursor values (e.g., “ms-float”), nor does it show OptimizedCursorPaginator.build_queryset or any code where a cursor value is compared to the datetime column. Therefore the specific claim about DateTimePaginator-issued cursors being “compared against the datetime column as a bare number” and cursors being non-interchangeable due to missing decoding is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — New `optimized_pagination` query flag is read straight from request.GET, bypassing AuditLogQueryParamSerializer, and is undocumented; it silently changes pagination semantics based on caller privilege with no schema or docs update.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `optimized_pagination` being read directly from `request.GET` (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) and used to switch paginator classes/behavior only for certain privileged users (`request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`). This introduces a new, unvalidated query flag that changes pagination semantics outside the existing query filtering/serialization path in this endpoint (the flag is not part of the `query` dict built earlier), which is a concrete review concern even if not a correctness bug by itself. The claim about being "undocumented"/"no schema update" is not verifiable from the diff, but the bypass/implicit behavior switch is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — Negative cursor offsets are now accepted as a public cursor input (`cursor=<v>:-N:0`) and passed to Django slicing, which raises AssertionError ("Negative indexing is not supported") and surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400 for malformed cursors.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/extends behavior where negative offsets can reach Django queryset slicing. In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, the updated `get_result` uses `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so for `cursor.is_prev` a negative `cursor.offset` will be used directly in `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Additionally, the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, again slicing `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing with a negative start commonly raises `AssertionError` (“Negative indexing is not supported”), and the diff shows no validation or error handling to convert that into a 4xx response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator now clamps negative non-prev offsets to 0 for every cursor-paginated endpoint, silently returning page 0 where a malformed cursor previously errored; this is an unannounced cross-endpoint behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` the slicing logic was changed from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, meaning negative `cursor.offset` values on non-`prev` cursors are now clamped to 0 and will return the first page instead of raising (Django queryset negative slicing previously errors). This is a cross-endpoint behavioral change for any code path using this paginator; the diff does not indicate any explicit cursor validation or announced behavior change, so it’s a real review concern but not necessarily a definite functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on a datetime (audit log key is "datetime"), raising TypeError in build_cursor for any non-empty page
matched_golden_ids: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: get_item_key/OptimizedCursorPaginator assumes the cursor key is numeric and applies math.floor/ceil, but the audit logs paginator orders by a datetime field, so using math.floor/ceil on a datetime raises a TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value which build_queryset injects into a raw SQL `datetime <= %s` comparison, producing a Postgres type error for any cursor with a value

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires `OptimizedCursorPaginator` into the audit log endpoint with `order_by="-datetime"` (a datetime field), but `OptimizedCursorPaginator`’s cursor/key logic is numeric: `get_item_key()` does `math.floor/ceil(value)` and returns an `int`, and `value_from_cursor()` returns `cursor.value` unchanged. If this paginator is used for a datetime-ordered queryset, cursor values/keys will be integers while the queryset filtering in `build_queryset(...)` (not shown here but invoked in `get_result`) will be based on the ordering key, creating a type mismatch (and even before that, `math.floor` on a datetime is invalid). This is a concrete incompatibility introduced by the diff, even if the finding’s exact “raw SQL `datetime <= %s`” phrasing isn’t directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — Negative cursor.offset is passed directly to queryset[start:stop]; Django QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported"), so the "advanced" branch always 500s instead of paginating

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the "advanced" path explicitly allows `cursor.offset < 0` and then slices the queryset with a negative start: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` where `start_offset = cursor.offset` (diff around the new class). Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices/offsets and will raise an exception rather than paginate, so this new branch is broken for the very condition it is meant to handle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member is None for non-member users (e.g. superusers or org-scoped tokens), so `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError whenever request.user.is_superuser is False

adjudication.rationale: The new logic computes `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. If `organization_context.member` can be `None`, this will raise `AttributeError` for non-superusers because the RHS is evaluated when `is_superuser` is False. The diff adds this dereference without a guard (e.g., `organization_context.member and ...`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — start/end/statsPeriod query params and the datetime__range filter were removed, so date-filtered requests now silently return unfiltered results

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `organization_auditlogs.py` only changes pagination behavior: it adds an `OptimizedCursorPaginator` option gated by `optimized_pagination` and admin access, but it does not show any removal of `start`, `end`, or `statsPeriod` query params nor any change/removal of a `datetime__range` filter. Based solely on the provided diff, the claimed regression (date-filtered requests becoming unfiltered) is not evidenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator still passes a negative offset to the slice when cursor.is_prev, so a crafted prev cursor with negative offset raises ValueError (500) while the same offset on a next cursor is silently clamped to 0

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` the new logic sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. If `cursor.is_prev` is true and `cursor.offset` is negative (which can come from a crafted cursor), `start_offset` remains negative and Django QuerySet slicing with a negative start raises an exception (typically ValueError/AssertionError), causing a 500. For the same negative offset when `cursor.is_prev` is false, it is clamped to 0 via `max(0, offset)`, matching the finding’s asymmetry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:891 — Trailing-row trim uses `offset + limit + extra` while results were fetched from start_offset..start_offset+limit+extra; when offset is negative the condition can never match and the extra row is not dropped

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is on and `cursor.offset < 0`, the slice is built as `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` and `stop = start_offset + limit + extra`, so a “full page” fetch would have `len(results) ~= limit + extra`. But the trailing-row trim later checks `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:` where `offset` is negative, making `offset + limit + extra < limit + extra` and thus the equality cannot hold. This prevents the `results = results[:-1]` drop from running in the negative-offset case, changing pagination behavior/cursor correctness for those requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — Gating a "privileged" pagination mode on `has_global_access` (true for ordinary org owners/managers, not just superusers) and a user-supplied `optimized_pagination` flag is security theater: it neither restricts nor protects anything, while suggesting that negative offsets are a privileged capability; the feature flag should not be user-controlled and the branch should be removed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds a user-controlled query parameter (`request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) to switch between `DateTimePaginator` and the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, and further gates “advanced” behavior on `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded design concern: the endpoint is now exposing a behavior switch directly to clients and tying it to a broad permission (`has_global_access`) rather than an internal/server-side feature flag. The finding’s characterization as “security theater” is partly subjective, but the underlying issue (user-controlled privileged-mode toggle + broad gating) is real and actionable from the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820 — New OptimizedCursorPaginator class (~95 lines, negative-offset path, is_prev path, cursor round-trip) ships with zero tests; the commit touches no test files at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a substantial new paginator implementation (`OptimizedCursorPaginator` in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, ~95 lines) including special-case negative-offset slicing and `is_prev` handling, and wires it into `organization_auditlogs.py` behind a query param plus an admin-only gate. The PR diff shows no changes to any test files, so this new nontrivial pagination logic ships without accompanying tests in this commit.
